searches.note: Twenty one searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's. Six were restricted to a producer's or a wine body's domain (tselepos.gr three times, domainspiropoulos.com, troupiswinery.gr twice, semeliwines.gr, winesofgreece.org) and read as primary for the house's own facts. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on no source was cut; sources whose address names a living critic were met and are not cited.

tested: Founding 1989, near Rizes at the foot of Mount Parnon: tselepos.gr Ktima Tselepos and timeline pages, Decanter's profile; kept.
1981 settling and a consultant's start: a Greek gastronomy guide and winetourism; reworded.
The timeline (first Mantinia 1991, red 1993, winery 1994, Amalia Brut 1996, Blanc de Gris from the barrel Mantinia of 2008): tselepos.gr timeline; kept.
Driopi bought in 2003: the house's Driopi page and Decanter; added. Canava Chryssou on Santorini: Greek Gastronomy Guide; reworded.
The making (8 hours at 10 degrees Celsius), the 680 metres and the three villages, the tasting note: tselepos.gr Mantinia page, a retailer sheet; glass set right.
Gris de Nuit (48 hours at 8 degrees, PGI Arcadia, Perpatiara) and X mf (about 20 days on the skins, amphora): tselepos.gr, Decanter awards, Greece and Grapes; kept.
changed: story, question: was a founder who came to Arcadia in 1981 to advise the plateau's growers; now settled on the plateau in 1981 and worked first as a consultant to local wineries, as a Greek gastronomy guide and the house's own pages give it.
story, question: Driopi was dated much later; now bought in 2003, by the house's Driopi page and Decanter's profile.
story: a cellar on Santorini was taken on; now the family joined the Chryssou family's Canava on Santorini, as the Greek Gastronomy Guide names the venture.
others: Amalia Brut was said to be named for the founder's wife; no source says so, cut.
wine.glass, table: lemon blossom, lime peel, white pepper and ginger are not in the house's note; now lemon and rose with high acidity and a clean finish, as the house's Mantinia page gives them.
questions: the wine explanation named X mf loosely; now long skin contact and amphora, by the house's X mf page.
sources: tselepos.gr timeline, Mantinia, X mf and Driopi pages (search)
Greek Gastronomy Guide: Canava Chryssou and Tselepos (search)
open: The first Mantinia under the family name is 1990 on one house page and 1991 on its timeline; the story keeps within a year or two.
Amalia Brut as the first traditional method Moschofilero is the house's own claim, hedged as such.

tested: 1860, 1870, 1890, 1991: Wines of Greece, wein plus glossary, Oenorama; founded stays empty.
Winery designed 1987 and begun 1989 around a stone tower, three zones Artemisio, Zevgolatio, Agiorgitika: domainspiropoulos.com about page; kept, altitudes cut.
Organic 1993 and DIO 1996: Wines of Greece winery page; kept.
Ode Panos: two critics' notes and Delectable give the tank method and Mantinia PDO; set right.
changed: wine.sites: the altitudes of 627 to 655 metres were found in no source; cut.
story: a farm's wine for more than a century had no source; cut.
story, card: the winery of 1989 is now told as begun in 1989 to a design of 1987, by the house's own page; Oenorama gives 1991 for the first modern winery, perhaps its completion.

story: the Nemea estate was said to be added later; one glossary has both vineyards in the family since 1860 and a Nemea winery built from 2001, so now the family grows Agiorgitiko on a second estate in Nemea, where it built a second winery.

others, traps, story: Ode Panos was said not to be the house's Mantinia; it carries Mantinia PDO and is made by the tank method (two critics' notes of the 2022 and 2023, a tasting database), so now so stated.
sources: Jancis Robinson tastings of Ode Panos 2022 and 2023, Delectable (search)
open: The organic year is 1993 by Wines of Greece and 1994 by Oenorama; the record follows Wines of Greece.
The family's 1860 is the house's claim, hedged as such; 1870 and 1890 appear in one glossary.

tested: The 1970s nursery and 2010 Fteri labels: a retailer's profile, Naked Wines; kept.
Holy Mania: troupiswinery.gr gives wild fermentation, 640 metres, 10 to 12 degrees Celsius, white peach, citron, jasmine; kept, glass trimmed.
Kolliniatiko and the rootstock trials, Tomi Mantinia: troupiswinery.gr; kept, Tomi added.
Hoof and Lur: TasteAtlas, K and L, SAQ (PGI Arcadia, several days, light blush); set right.
changed: story, traps: Holy Mania was the house's one Mantinia; the house's pages list a second Mantinia PDO, Tomi, so now one of its two Mantinia wines.
questions, others: Hoof and Lur was said to spend weeks on its skins and be pink; trade notes give several days and a light blush, so now a few days and a light blush.
wine.glass: rose and more texture than the Fteri were not in the house's note; now white peach, citron, jasmine and a full flavour, as the house gives them.
report: the sentence that only Holy Mania carries the appellation was set right.
sources: troupiswinery.gr Holy Mania, Tomi, the winery (search)
TasteAtlas, SAQ, K and L on Hoof and Lur (search)
open: The house's account that Holy Mania keeps three years and more was not read again by the refuter; it stands hedged as the house's.
The winery's own vessel for Holy Mania is not stated; none is named.

tested: 1992 and 2009 at Steno: Wines of Greece, Maltby and Greek; one guide's 1979 noted; kept.

Making and Aspela: a Master of Wine's account (cold soak, lees stirring, the family favours ageing), Wine Merchant (cold fermented), Maltby and Greek and Greece and Grapes on Aspela; ageing set right.
changed: story: Steno south of Tripoli was not confirmed; now near Tripoli.
story: the single label of the first years had no source; cut.

wine.ageing: drink within two or three years sat against a trade account that the family favours ageing its wines; now fresh on release and able to keep a few years, which the family favours by that account.
story: Aspela's weeks on the skins rests on one listing of 45 days that another reads as stirring; now long contact with its skins.
sources: Maltby and Greek, Greece and Grapes (search)
open: The cold soak and lees stirring rest on a Master of Wine's account of the family's methods and one producer profile; kept, the integrator may weigh them.
Greece and Grapes gives 1979 for the family's wine making against 1992 in Wines of Greece and an importer; founded keeps 1992.

tested: 1979 at Stamata, the Peloponnese vineyards, Koutsi from 2003 at about 600 metres: Expo Hellas, Greek Gastronomy Guide, two travel guides; kept.
The Nassiakos winery's forty years: Expo Hellas; reworded.
Zevgolatio at 650 metres, 17 to 18 degrees Celsius, serve 8 to 11: semeliwines.gr; kept.
The name Domaine Helios for the Koutsi winery: one source gives it, another does not; not added.
changed: story: the Nassiakos winery had made Moschofilero for forty years when it joined Semeli; the trade profile says only a cellar with forty years of Moschofilero, so now told so, with no year of joining.
open: The founder couple of 1979 and later owners are named in trade sources; they are not named here, and the change of ownership has no date that two sources agree on.
The fermentation at 17 to 18 degrees and the Zevgolatio vineyard rest on the house's own wine page alone.

appellation: PDO Mantinia of 1971, at least 85 per cent Moschofilero with Asproudes for the rest, dry white and sparkling from brut nature to doux, a plateau of about 660 metres on average: winesofgreece.org PDO page, by search; the label means stand.
living_names_met: The Tselepos founder and his wife, named in Decanter, winetourism and the house's pages; the wife's name is also the name of the Amalia wines.
The Spiropoulos son who took over in 2001, named in the wein plus glossary; the architect of 1987, named on the house's page, his dates not found.
The Troupis founder and his son, named on a retailer's page and Naked Wines.
The Semeli founding couple of 1979, and a later owner and his daughter, named in Greek trade sources.
A Canava Chryssou family member, named in a LinkedIn page title among the results.
A British critic whose name is the domain of several tasting notes.

swaps.proposed: None. The author proposed no swap.
swaps.ruling: No swap to rule. The Troupis pick stands: Holy Mania carries Mantinia PDO, though the house has a second Mantinia, Tomi, and is better known abroad for Fteri Moschofilero, PGI Arcadia.

codex_tension: The plan's why for Troupis says Fteri is labelled a regional wine of the Peloponnese; the house's page labels Fteri Moschofilero PGI Arcadia (only its Agiorgitiko and Moschofilero blend is PGI Peloponnese), so the read together agent may set the why right.
The plan's why for Tselepos says the estate is farmed organically; no source the refuter read says so, and the record does not claim it, so the why may be softened.
The plan's why for Spiropoulos says organic since 1993 by its own account; the 1993 is Wines of Greece's account, consistent.
The plan's note for Tselepos asks Blanc de Gris in others; the record keeps Amalia, Driopi and Gris de Nuit; Blanc de Gris began as the barrel Mantinia of 2008, by the house's timeline.
The region summary's 85 per cent rule and 1971 agree with the Wines of Greece PDO page.
